title: P3-06 — OpenUI cards in folded conversation turn tails, verified in a real browser

environment.profile: p3web — isolated DSH_HOME at tmp/dsh-p3 on :3093; production desktop (:61582) untouched
environment.browser: Chromium Agent Window (browser-skill over CDP), session lnzp

method.noCssOverrides: No display property was set by any script in this run. The page's own computed styles decide every verdict; `noOverrides` in the acceptance step asserts no capture marker is present.
method.visibilityRule: A card counts as visible only when it has a non-zero box inside the viewport AND no ancestor reports `content-visibility` other than `visible`. The host uses `content-visibility: hidden` on fold containers, so this rule distinguishes 'in the tail' from 'inside the collapsed process' without touching the host.
method.whyThisMattered: The previous phase's screenshots forced `content-visibility: visible` on host containers to photograph a card that was laid out but never painted. This phase does not need that, because the card is genuinely outside the fold.

checks.name: a freshly drawn OpenUI card is visible without expanding the fold
checks.detail: Turn tail mounted its own copy of each program card: surfaces split 3 inside folds / 3 outside. Before P3-06 the OpenUI turns produced no tail copy at all.

checks.name: the persisted value survives the reload and is visible folded
checks.detail: Dragged the TAIL copy 6 -> 8; after a full reload the tail card still showed 'count 8' with slider value 8, and the record was {v:1,h:18bcb949,values:{count:8}}.

checks.name: expanding the fold does not duplicate a card in the tail
checks.detail: After expanding, the total stayed 4 and the split stayed 2 in the fold / 2 in the tail. The toolview copy is the call's record inside the fold; the tail keeps exactly one copy. This is the policy the HTML backend already had.

checks.name: an interaction in the tail card drives its siblings and persists
checks.detail: Setting the tail card's Slider to 8 changed its Text to 'count 8' and wrote the record; the same key is read by the toolview copy.

checks.name: the HTML backend's turn-tail behaviour is unchanged
checks.detail: The HTML control card produced two surfaces: one inside the fold, one outside it in the tail — the same shape it had before this change, now measured explicitly.

checks.name: no host CSS was modified to make any of this visible
checks.detail: The acceptance step asserts no capture marker remains in the DOM and that all folds report aria-expanded=false while two tail cards are visible.

checks.name: session switching shows no other session's cards or state
checks.detail: Unit-tested (tests/turn-cards.spec.tsx 'keeps two sessions apart on the turn tail'), not driven live: the browser run stayed in one session.

checks.name: a legacy pre-fork dsh-intelligent-ui card replays on the turn tail
checks.detail: The reader path is unit-tested (a program-shaped descriptor is accepted by `visualizationFrom` and rejected by the old `visualizeMetaFrom`), but no genuine pre-fork card exists in an isolated session to replay.

defectFoundDuringVerification.what: The isolated profile served a STALE build for the first round of P3-06 measurements.
defectFoundDuringVerification.why: `dsh plugin add file:...` copies lib/ at install time. The P3-06 build happened after that install, so the profile kept the pre-fix bundle and the turn tail correctly showed nothing for OpenUI.
defectFoundDuringVerification.howDetected: The installed lib/client.js hash differed from the worktree build, and a grep found 4 matches for the new symbols in the installed copy against 7 in the worktree build.
defectFoundDuringVerification.resolution: Copied the fresh lib/ into the profile, restarted, and re-ran every measurement. All results above are from the corrected build.
defectFoundDuringVerification.lesson: A 'fails in browser but passes in tests' reading must be checked against what the browser actually loaded before it is reported as a code defect.
